name: Serum Institute of India
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Manufactures vaccines, antisera and biopharmaceuticals, and is the world's largest vaccine maker by doses produced.
capacity_detail: Valued at Rs 2,11,610 crore, ranked No. 2 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500 (Feb 2025); FY22 revenue Rs 25,646 crore (USD 3.47bn)
markets: Vaccines supplied worldwide, including WHO, UNICEF and PAHO programmes; malaria vaccine licensed in Ghana, Nigeria and Burkina Faso.
rationale: Cash-rich global vaccine leader controlled by the Poonawalla family; F1 would lift a B2G brand into a premium global corporate profile.

name: Zoho Corporation
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Develops cloud business software for sales, marketing, customer service, finance and security, used by over a million organisations.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 123.13bn (USD 1.5bn) in FY2025; valued at Rs 1,03,760 crore in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500
markets: Over 120 million users across more than a million organisations worldwide, with offices in Chennai and Austin, Texas.
rationale: Bootstrapped SaaS rival of Salesforce, Oracle and Freshworks, all F1 partners; a team deal would match their B2B visibility.

name: Parle Products
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes Parle-G, Monaco, Krackjack, Hide & Seek and Melody biscuits and confectionery, selling across India and abroad.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 17,223 crore (USD 1.8bn) in FY23
markets: Mass-market biscuits sold throughout India with worldwide distribution; Parle-G named the world's best-selling biscuit brand by Nielsen.
rationale: Chauhan-family FMCG giant ranked among India's most valuable unlisted firms; F1's Indian fan growth suits mass consumer brand building.

name: Amul (Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation)
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Markets Amul milk, butter, cheese, ice cream and dairy products for a co-operative of 3.6 million milk producers.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 90,000 crore (USD 9.6bn) in 2025
sponsorships: Official partner of Kolkata Knight Riders (IPL, since 2021) and Punjab Kings (IPL 2026); Amul Protein partner of Delhi Capitals (IPL 2026)
markets: India nationwide; fresh milk launched in the United States (2024) and Spain (2025); cheese exports to the Middle East and Asia.
rationale: India's largest food brand is expanding milk sales into the US and Europe; F1 offers matching global reach and visibility.

name: Bharat Biotech
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Develops and manufactures vaccines including Covaxin, Rotavac and Typbar TCV, registered in over 125 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 8,148 crore (USD 870m) in FY22
markets: Vaccine registrations in over 125 countries and more than nine billion doses delivered worldwide as of May 2025.
rationale: Profitable private vaccine maker selling worldwide; F1 corporate hospitality could support government and partner relationships across markets.

name: Biological E
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Manufactures low-cost vaccines including pentavalent and Corbevax for WHO, UNICEF and international aid programmes.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 3,820 crore (USD 410m) in FY23
markets: India plus supply to WHO, UNICEF and Gates Foundation programmes in low- and middle-income countries.
rationale: Datla-family vaccine maker with global contract work; F1 is a long shot but could support international partnership hospitality.

name: Himalaya Wellness Company
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes herbal pharmaceuticals, personal care, baby care, nutrition and animal health products including Liv.52 and Himalaya Neem face wash.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 37.6bn (USD 400m) in FY22
markets: Products sold in 106 countries, with regional head offices in Dubai, Singapore and Houston serving the US, Middle East, Asia, Europe and Oceania.
rationale: Herbal wellness brand already selling in 106 countries; F1's global broadcast reach suits building its consumer personal care lines abroad.

name: Parle Agro
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes packaged beverages and snacks including Frooti, Appy Fizz, Smoodh, Bailley water and Hippo, sold from India.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 3,126 crore (USD 330m) in FY24
markets: India nationwide, with its area served listed as worldwide.
rationale: Youth-focused drinks brand competing with PepsiCo and Red Bull, both F1 partners; an F1 tie-in would fit Appy Fizz-style lifestyle marketing.

name: Bisleri International
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Sells Bisleri packaged drinking water, Vedica mineral water and Limonata, Rev and Pop soft drinks across India and the UAE.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 9,830 crore, No. 492 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; also hydration partner of IPL teams
sponsorships: Hydration partner of five IPL teams and five ISL clubs; Punjab Kings and Delhi Capitals official hydration partner (IPL 2026)
markets: India through 150 plants and 6,000 distributors, with expansion into the United Arab Emirates in 2023.
rationale: Already a heavy IPL sponsor; an F1 hydration partnership would extend its premium Vedica water ambitions internationally.

name: IFFCO (Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative)
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Produces urea, DAP, NPK and other fertilisers for Indian farmers as a multi-state co-operative with insurance and agrochemical ventures.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 42,662 crore (USD 4.6bn) in FY25
markets: India mainly, with fertiliser ventures in Oman, Jordan, Senegal and a trading arm in Dubai.
rationale: Very large co-operative with rural Indian focus; F1 is unlikely beyond corporate hospitality for its nano-fertiliser export push.

name: DS Group (Dharampal Satyapal)
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes Catch spices, Pass Pass and Pulse confectionery, Rajnigandha mouth fresheners and owns Lalique and luxury hospitality brands.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 5,500 crore (USD 590m) in 2023
markets: India nationwide with worldwide sales, including the Lalique Group's luxury business in Europe.
rationale: Brand-led FMCG group with a European luxury arm; F1 hospitality and visibility fit its Lalique and premium food ambitions.

name: Bennett, Coleman & Co. (Times Group)
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Publishes The Times of India and The Economic Times and runs Times Now, Radio Mirchi and Times Internet.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 73.94bn (USD 790m) in 2022
markets: India: print, TV, radio and digital media, including Cricbuzz and Willow cricket platforms.
rationale: India's largest media house could take an F1 media partnership to grow motorsport content on its sports and business channels.

name: Godrej & Boyce
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes aerospace parts, appliances, Godrej Interio furniture, locks, security systems and material-handling equipment for Indian and export markets.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 11,800 crore (USD 1.3bn) in 2021-22
markets: India with products sold in Europe, the US, Middle East, Africa and South East Asia.
rationale: Engineering-led group with aerospace and appliance brands; F1 technology storytelling suits its Godrej Aerospace and premium appliance ambitions.

name: Wipro Enterprises
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Owns Santoor, Yardley and Chandrika personal care brands, lighting and hydraulic and aerospace engineering businesses, separate from Wipro Limited.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 16,934 crore (USD 1.8bn) in FY24
markets: India and South East Asia consumer brands, plus engineering in South Africa, China, Sweden, Brazil, Romania and Israel.
rationale: Azim Premji-owned consumer group with Asian personal care brands like Yardley; F1 Asian races could support regional brand building.

name: MAS Holdings
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Designs and manufactures lingerie, swimwear, activewear and smart textiles for global brands, plus its own amantè and Ultimo labels.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2bn in 2018
markets: 53 manufacturing facilities in 17 countries, supplying Nike, Speedo and Marks & Spencer, with amantè sold in India.
rationale: South Asia's largest apparel maker supplies sportswear giants; F1 visibility could support its activewear and own-brand ambitions with Western buyers.

name: Brandix
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Manufactures casualwear, intimatewear, loungewear and activewear for international brands and owns Moose Clothing and IT firm Fortude.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 820m in 2020-21 (Brandix Sustainability Report)
sponsorships: Moose Clothing co-sponsor of South Africa cricket tour of Sri Lanka (2018)
markets: Operations in Sri Lanka, India, Bangladesh and Cambodia, with offices in the US, UK, Australia, Singapore and Hong Kong.
rationale: Large apparel exporter with activewear lines; F1 hospitality could strengthen relationships with Western brand customers and promote Moose locally.

name: Amalgamations Group (TAFE)
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Family group whose flagship TAFE makes Massey Ferguson India, Eicher and TAFE tractors, exported to over 80 countries.
capacity_detail: Amalgamations valued at INR 56,660 crore, 10th most valuable unlisted company in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; TAFE turnover above Rs 13,700 crore
markets: India with tractor exports to over 80 countries.
rationale: Valuable engineering group competing with Mahindra and John Deere; F1 engineering prestige could support TAFE's own-brand tractor exports.

name: Meghna Group of Industries
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Bangladeshi conglomerate making Fresh-branded cement, edible oil, sugar, ceramics, LPG, paper and diapers, with media and shipping interests.
capacity_detail: Revenue BDT 200bn (USD 2.5bn) in 2017
markets: Bangladesh, with manufacturing in three economic zones and consumer brands sold nationwide.
rationale: One of Bangladesh's biggest groups; F1 is a long shot, mainly for corporate prestige and hospitality.

name: Jaquar Group
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes bathroom fittings, showers, sanitaryware and lighting under the Artize, Jaquar and Essco brands for homes and projects.
capacity_detail: Revenue about USD 1bn (INR 8,703 crore) in 2025-26
markets: Operates in over 55 countries across Europe, the Middle East, South East Asia, Africa and the SAARC region.
rationale: Premium bathroom brand selling in 55 countries; F1 luxury positioning and Middle East races suit its Artize push against European rivals.

name: Cadila Pharmaceuticals
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes active pharmaceutical ingredients, generic formulations and biotech products, with contract research and manufacturing services.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 3,675 crore (USD 390m) in FY23
markets: India, with USFDA-certified plants serving export markets and a WHO-compliant plant in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
rationale: Modi-family pharma with export plants; F1 is a long shot beyond hospitality for international pharma partners.

name: Mother Dairy
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Sells Mother Dairy milk and dairy products, Safal fruit, vegetables and frozen foods, and Dhara edible oil.
capacity_detail: Revenue over Rs 17,000 crore as of 2026
markets: Mainly Delhi NCR (over 65% of 2025 sales); Safal products present in about 40 countries.
rationale: Large consumer dairy brand; F1 is a long shot, though Safal exports could use international visibility.

name: Kolkata Knight Riders (Knight Riders Group)
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Owns the Kolkata Knight Riders IPL team and Knight Riders franchises in the Caribbean, UAE and US cricket leagues.
ownership: private: Shah Rukh Khan (55%), Mehta Group (45%)
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 20,850 crore, No. 270 in the 2025 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500 (June 2026)
markets: India (IPL), Trinidad and Tobago (CPL), Abu Dhabi (ILT20) and Los Angeles (Major League Cricket).
rationale: Global cricket franchise network with celebrity owners; cross-promotion with an F1 team could reach both sports' fans in India, the Gulf and US.

name: Chennai Super Kings
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Owns and operates the Chennai Super Kings Indian Premier League cricket team through Chennai Super Kings Cricket Limited.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 19,550 crore, No. 285 in the 2025 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500 (June 2026)
markets: India, through the IPL; front-of-shirt sponsor Etihad Airways since 2025.
rationale: Most popular IPL brand shares sponsors such as Etihad with F1; a content or fan partnership with a team is plausible.

name: Rajasthan Royals
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Owns and operates the Rajasthan Royals Indian Premier League cricket team, bought by a Mittal-Poonawalla consortium in 2026.
ownership: private: Lakshmi Mittal (75%), Adar Poonawalla (18%), Manoj Badale (7%)
capacity_detail: Acquired by a consortium led by Lakshmi Mittal and Adar Poonawalla for USD 1.65bn (May 2026)
markets: India, through the Indian Premier League.
rationale: New billionaire owners may seek international profile; joint fan and content deals with an F1 team are plausible.

name: Punjab Kings
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Owns and operates the Punjab Kings Indian Premier League cricket team, jointly owned by Burman, Wadia, Zinta and Paul.
ownership: private: Mohit Burman (48%), Ness Wadia (23%), Preity Zinta (23%), Karan Paul (6%)
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 14,050 crore, No. 390 in the 2025 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500 (June 2026)
markets: India, through the Indian Premier League.
rationale: Valuable IPL franchise; F1 fit is limited to cross-promotion and hospitality.

name: Ha-Meem Group
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Manufactures and exports ready-made garments, mainly to the United States, and sells clothing in Bangladesh.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 550m (year not stated on page)
markets: Bangladesh domestic sales plus garment exports, about 80 per cent of them to the United States.
rationale: Large garment exporter dependent on US buyers; F1 is a long shot, useful mainly for buyer hospitality at US races.

name: Megha Engineering & Infrastructures (MEIL)
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Builds expressways, tunnels, irrigation pump houses, ports and power projects across India as an engineering and construction contractor.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 77,860 crore, No. 88 overall and 5th most valuable unlisted company in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500
markets: India: highways, tunnels, irrigation, ports and energy infrastructure projects.
rationale: One of India's most valuable private firms; F1 fit is weak beyond corporate hospitality and brand prestige.

name: Usha International
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Sells Usha sewing machines, fans, kitchen appliances, coolers, water heaters and TISVA lighting across India.
capacity_detail: Sponsor of Mumbai Indians in the Indian Premier League and Women's Premier League
sponsorships: Mumbai Indians (IPL and WPL); Ladies Amateur Open Golf; Usha Play traditional sports
markets: Pan-India network of branches and company stores, strong in tier-2 and tier-3 cities.
rationale: Shriram-family appliance brand already spending on IPL; F1's growing Indian audience suits premium fan and appliance lines.

name: Saraswat Co-operative Bank
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Provides retail and business banking through over 300 branches as one of India's largest urban co-operative banks.
capacity_detail: Revenue Rs 3,552.58 crore (USD 380m) in 2022-23
markets: India, mainly Maharashtra, with over 300 branches and 350 ATMs; business of Rs 91,814 crore in FY2024-25.
rationale: Large co-operative bank with regional focus; F1 is unlikely beyond client hospitality.

name: Shahi Exports
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: One of India's largest apparel makers and exporters, producing over 150 million garments a year across 50 factories.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 24,330 crore, No. 243 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500 (named an unlisted new entrant)
markets: Garment exports from 50 factories and 5 textile mills across 8 Indian states, with over 100,000 employees.
rationale: Major supplier to global apparel brands; F1 hospitality could strengthen buyer relationships, though consumer visibility matters little.

name: Aparna Constructions and Estates
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Develops premium gated residential communities, apartments, plots and commercial property in Hyderabad and Bengaluru.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 29,400 crore, No. 204 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500 (named an unlisted new entrant)
markets: Hyderabad residential projects in Gachibowli, Kompally and Tellapur, with an office in Bengaluru.
rationale: Premium developer marketing to affluent buyers; F1 is a long shot beyond luxury positioning and hospitality.

name: USV Private Limited
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Pharmaceutical, cosmeceutical and nutraceutical company making branded drugs, generics and biosimilars for India and international markets.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 28,390 crore, No. 208 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500
markets: India business plus an international business in generics and biosimilars; countries not detailed on its site.
rationale: Valuable private pharma group; F1 fit limited to corporate hospitality and international partner relations.

name: Kiran Gems
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Cuts and exports polished natural diamonds as a De Beers sightholder, describing itself as the world's largest manufacturer.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 21,050 crore, No. 271 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500
markets: Manufacturing in Mumbai and Surat; offices in Dubai and New York; sales in Hong Kong, China, Belgium, Australia and the US.
rationale: Global diamond supplier; F1's luxury audience and Gulf and US races could support a natural-diamond marketing push.

name: Paharpur Cooling Towers
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes wet and dry cooling towers, air-cooled condensers and heat exchangers for power and industrial plants worldwide.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 10,560 crore, No. 462 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; unlisted company CIN U02005WB1949PLC018363
markets: Over 82,000 cooling towers and heat exchangers sold worldwide, with a factory in Zhangjiakou, China.
rationale: Engineering exporter to power plants; F1 offers little beyond B2B hospitality.

name: Hetero
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes APIs, generic drugs and biosimilars, including HIV and COVID-19 antivirals and generic semaglutide, sold in over 145 countries.
capacity_detail: Hetero Labs valued at INR 31,580 crore, No. 194 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500
markets: Operations in over 145 countries, with a commercial office opened in Warsaw, Poland in 2025.
rationale: Global generics player expanding in Europe; F1 fit is weak beyond corporate hospitality.

name: T-Series (Super Cassettes Industries)
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: India's largest music label and a film producer, running the world's most-subscribed YouTube channel.
capacity_detail: Super Cassettes Industries valued at INR 23,210 crore, No. 252 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500
markets: India plus global YouTube audience; about 40% of channel traffic comes from outside India, including 12% from the US.
rationale: Massive global digital audience; music and content collaborations with an F1 team could reach young South Asian fans worldwide.

name: Macleods Pharmaceuticals
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Develops and manufactures APIs and generic formulations, including WHO-prequalified medicines, for India and export markets.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 52,150 crore, No. 125 and among the top 10 bootstrapped companies in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500
markets: Offices in India, Indonesia, the US, UK, South Africa, Kazakhstan, Spain, Ukraine, MENA, Germany and the Netherlands.
rationale: Large global generics maker; F1 is a long shot beyond hospitality for international partners.

name: Rubamin
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Recycles lithium-ion batteries, spent catalysts and zinc to recover strategic metals such as lithium, nickel, cobalt and molybdenum.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 11,360 crore, No. 437 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; Rubamin Pvt. Ltd., CIN U24299GJ1987PTC009942
markets: India-based recycling plants supplying recovered metals to global catalyst manufacturers.
rationale: Battery-recycling growth story; F1's sustainability and hybrid-power narrative could showcase its critical-metals circular economy credentials.

name: Viraj Profiles
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Manufactures stainless steel wire rods, wires, fasteners, bright bars, profiles, flanges and welding wires for export.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 16,220 crore, No. 348 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; Viraj Profiles Pvt. Ltd.
markets: Exports stainless steel long products to more than 90 countries.
rationale: Export-led industrial supplier; F1 fit is weak beyond B2B hospitality.

name: Colourtex Industries
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes textile and non-textile dyes, eco-friendly reactive dyes and organic pigments for the global textile industry.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 14,390 crore, No. 379 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; Colourtex Industries Pvt. Ltd.
markets: Serves global textile industries from India; partner of DuPont Artistri inks.
rationale: Specialty chemicals exporter; F1 offers little beyond customer hospitality.

name: BDR Pharmaceuticals International
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Develops niche APIs, generic formulations and modified-release pellets, specialising in water-soluble oncology products.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 11,950 crore, No. 419 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; BDR Pharmaceuticals International Pvt Ltd
markets: India plus partners across Africa, Asia, Europe, North America and South America.
rationale: Specialty oncology generics maker; F1 is a long shot beyond hospitality.

name: Shree Ramkrishna Exports (SRK)
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Crafts and exports natural polished diamonds and jewellery, with traceability and grading systems, as a De Beers sightholder.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 15,700 crore, No. 357 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; Shree Ramkrishna Exports Pvt. Ltd.
markets: Two natural diamond crafting facilities in India; sightholder of De Beers, Alrosa and Rio Tinto; exhibits in Hong Kong.
rationale: Dholakia family diamond house with luxury jewellery ambitions; F1's affluent global audience could support its Pure Luxury brand.

name: Farmson Pharmaceuticals
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Produces paracetamol and caffeine APIs and other bulk drugs, holding 23% of the global paracetamol API market.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 9,670 crore, No. 496 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; group company Farmson Basic Drugs Private Limited
markets: Supplies over 400 partners in more than 65 countries.
rationale: Bulk drug supplier with little consumer exposure; F1 fit is weak.

name: Chettinad Cement Corporation
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes cement at plants in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Telangana for South Indian builders.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 12,160 crore, No. 416 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; Chettinad Cement Corporation Private Limited
markets: South and west India, serving clients including Tata Group, Larsen & Toubro and ISRO.
rationale: Regional cement maker; F1 has little relevance beyond hospitality.

name: Aristo Pharmaceuticals
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Markets branded medicines such as Monocef, Pantop and Mikacin, ranking among India's top ten Indian-owned pharma firms by turnover.
capacity_detail: Valued at INR 33,320 crore, No. 182 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; ARISTO Pharmaceuticals Private Limited
markets: Indian pharmaceutical market, strongest in anti-infectives, gastro-intestinal and cardiac medicines.
rationale: Large domestic pharma with doctor-focused marketing; F1 fit is weak.

name: Bagmane Group
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Develops and operates technology and business parks in Bengaluru, with about 30 million sq ft operational.
capacity_detail: Bagmane Developers valued at INR 18,680 crore, No. 296 in the 2024 Burgundy Private Hurun India 500; Bagmane Developers Private Limited
markets: Bengaluru: Bagmane Tech Park, World Technology Centre, Constellation Business Park and other campuses over 500 acres.
rationale: Office landlord to global tech tenants; F1 hospitality could court multinational occupiers, though brand fit is limited.

name: NIVIA Sports
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes and markets sports shoes, balls, sportswear and equipment for football, basketball, volleyball, cricket and fitness.
capacity_detail: Official sports gear partner of Punjab Kings in the Indian Premier League 2026
sponsorships: Punjab Kings (IPL 2026); Indian Super League match ball (2018-present); All India Football Federation (2018-present); Jamshedpur FC
markets: India with sponsorships and sales in Bhutan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Singapore and Liberia.
rationale: Home-grown sports brand already active in IPL and Indian football; F1 merchandise or fan-gear tie-ins could lift its premium image.

name: Livguard
group: Regional rankings: India and South Asia
desc: Makes home inverters, inverter and automotive batteries, lithium energy storage and solar products for Indian homes and vehicles.
capacity_detail: Exclusive power partner of Punjab Kings in the Indian Premier League 2026; Livguard Energy Technologies Private Limited (CIN U51909HR2014FTC091348)
markets: India, available across more than 21,000 pin codes, with a global operations arm.
rationale: Energy-storage brand spending on IPL; F1's hybrid and battery technology story offers a natural premium marketing platform.
